content.text: NONE ARE FOR USE IN CHILDREN <2YO
: sedation, cognitive dysfunction, dry mouth, blurred vision
-    MOA: H1-receptor antagonist (1st-gen, cross BBB) -> block CNS histamine wakefulness -> sedation (+ anticholinergic)

-    Caution: marked drowsiness (↑ w alcohol/sedatives/tranquilizers) · ask doctor first: breathing problems, glaucoma, trouble urinating (enlrg prostate) · ⍉ use to make a child sleepy · excitability (children)
- adults + children ≥12 y: 1-2 tabs (25 mg each)

content.text: : cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracellular receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synthesis of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from muscle/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits number/activity of cells involved in inflammatory response
Inhibits histamine release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/water retention, potassium loss
•Treatment of chronic inflammatory diseases:  skin inflammation
: increased appetite/weight gain, fluid retention, emotional instability, insomnia, indigestion, bitter taste, increased BP/BG

: osteoporosis, GI (ulceration, bleeding), psychiatric (mood, psychosis), cataracts, glaucoma, CV (HTN, edema, hypokalemia), diabetes, hyperlipidemia, Cushingoid syndrome, growth failure, impaired wound healing, adrenal suppression, immunosuppression
↑bone catabolism or antagonize vit D driven Ca absorb
Stim gastric acid & pepsin prod -> take w food
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal

: antimetabolite; interferes with DNA synthesis, repair, and cellular replication by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR); MOA in RA is unknown, but is thought to be similar to the antineoplastic action: folate antagonist that inhibits synthesis of purines
: pregnancy/lactating, alcoholism, hepatic disease, immunodeficiency syndromes, preexisting blood dyscrasias
: GI (N/V/D, stomatitis) alopecia, elevated serum transaminases, skin (rash, pruritis, urticaria), CNS (fatigue, HA, malaise)
•less common – bone marrow suppression, immunosuppression, interstitial pneumonitis, hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis
: derivative of 6-mercaptopurine and acts as an immunosuppressive antimetabolite
PO, SQ, IM, IV; folic acid supp → ↓AE

: synthetic purine nucleoside analog with activity against HSV (types 1 and 2), varicella-zoster virus (VZV), and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV); stops replication of herpes viral DNA by competitive inhibition of viral DNA polymerase (selective toxicity), incorporation into and termination of the growing viral DNA chain, and inactivation of the viral DNA polymerase
: IV (injection site inflammation or phlebitis, transient elevation of SCr/BUN, N/V), PO (GI disturbances, HA, skin rash)
: protein synthesis inhibitor (binds to 30S ribosomal subunit); bacteriostatic
•broad spectrum of activity – good against gram (+), gram (-), atypical organisms, & organisms other than bacteria
•poor GI tolerance: may cause diarrhea & gastritis
•deposition in calcified tissue: deposition in teeth causes teeth discoloration & may affect growth (not usually given in children <8yo for >21d)
•impaired absorption if given w/ dairy products, Ca, Al, Mg, Fe
